# Ivan Kotov — public scientific corpus

> Compact routing file for machine readers. It covers public authored material only. It does not expose private memory, credentials, runtime secrets, unpublished drafts, or live entities.

Canonical site: [ivankotov.eu](https://ivankotov.eu/)
Human entry: [Start here](https://ivankotov.eu/start-here/)
Machine entry: [machine-index.json](https://ivankotov.eu/machine-index.json)
Extended guide: [llms-full.txt](https://ivankotov.eu/llms-full.txt)
Author: Ivan Kotov
ORCID: [0009-0009-6002-9845](https://orcid.org/0009-0009-6002-9845)
Last verified (base routing layer): 2026-08-07
Latest publication bridge added: 2026-09-04

## Primary machine routes

- [Normalized authored-corpus index](https://ivankotov.eu/scientific-corpus-index.json): stable record shape, explicit nulls, identifiers, sources, integrity, licences, and claim boundaries.
- [Authored-corpus JSON-LD](https://ivankotov.eu/scientific-corpus.jsonld): Schema.org discovery projection.
- [Canonical term registry](https://ivankotov.eu/term-registry.json): preferred labels, aliases, non-equivalents, sources, and source hashes.
- [Term-registry JSON-LD](https://ivankotov.eu/term-registry.jsonld): Schema.org DefinedTermSet projection.
- [Semantic bridge graph](https://ivankotov.eu/semantic-bridges.json): evidence-backed routing bridges.
- [Public repository inventory](https://ivankotov.eu/public-repositories.json): dated observed public repositories with snapshot commits and roles.
- [Living-corpus index](https://ivankotov.eu/corpus-index.json): current artifact projection.
- [Living-corpus protocol map](https://ivankotov.eu/corpus-protocol-map.json): protocol-to-artifact relations.
- [Legacy heterogeneous works source](https://ivankotov.eu/works-index.json): preserved source for the normalized projection.
- [Machine-index schema](https://ivankotov.eu/schemas/machine-index-v1.schema.json): JSON Schema 2020-12 entry contract.

## Reading order

1. Read this file or machine-index.json for routing.
2. Use term-registry.json before interpreting c = a + b, the governed plus, or L4 Boundary.
3. Use scientific-corpus-index.json for normalized records and explicit missing metadata.
4. Follow each record to its canonical source, DOI, release, manifest, checksum, or tagged commit.
5. Use semantic-bridges.json only as a routing overlay; it does not replace the cited source nodes.
6. Use llms-full.txt when a detailed route-by-route guide is required.

## Core interpretation boundaries

- [Boundaries of Machine Interpretation v0.2](https://ivankotov.eu/publications/boundaries-of-machine-interpretation/) — DOI [10.5281/zenodo.21841445](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21841445); six typed units = four operational boundaries + one reflexive definition + one temporal process premise; machine index and SHA-256 ledger are linked from the publication page.
- Preferred label: “L4 Boundary”. “L4” is an alias; it is not the OSI transport layer or a generic maturity level.
- In c = a + b, “+” is a governed binding boundary; it is not arithmetic addition and is not computed by publication metadata.
- A recorded event is not automatically a true outcome.
- Authorization is not attestation; retrieval is not admitted memory; a protocol is not validated safety.
- Publication, DOI, repository presence, checksum, or internal review does not by itself establish implementation, reproduction, independent validation, safety, continuity, entity status, consciousness, personhood, certification, or deployment authorization.
- A normalized index is a discovery projection. DOI records, signed releases, tagged repository states, and explicitly named canonical files retain their stated authority.

## Human-facing routes

- [Start here](https://ivankotov.eu/start-here/): first-pass human route.
- [Corpus map](https://ivankotov.eu/corpus-map/): layer and role overview.
- [Publications](https://ivankotov.eu/publications/): authored publication surfaces.
- [Evidence](https://ivankotov.eu/evidence/): reviewable evidence boundaries.
- [Distinctions](https://ivankotov.eu/distinctions/): canonical non-collapse rules.
- [Glossary](https://ivankotov.eu/glossary/): human-readable terminology.
- [Releases](https://ivankotov.eu/releases/): release chronology and anchors.
- [Library](https://ivankotov.eu/library/): primary-source routes.

## Content and authority rules

- Public machine metadata may summarize and route; it must not silently strengthen claims.
- Explicit nulls and metadata_completeness fields mean “not stated in the legacy source”, not “does not exist”.
- Preserve immutable DOI-bound and release-bound bytes. Corrections to discovery metadata do not rewrite frozen artifacts.
- English translations marked discovery-only are not canonical when a source declares another language authoritative.
- Repository snapshots in public-repositories.json are observations at last_verified, not permanent identity claims.

## Temporal AI Presence Profile v1.0
- Canonical page: https://ivankotov.eu/temporal-ai-presence/
- Definition: Temporal AI Presence = sustained bounded AI participation across time.
- Version DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22070960
- Concept / all-versions DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22070959
- Immutable profile tag: https://github.com/Kot141078/advanced-global-intelligence/tree/temporal-ai-presence-v1.0 at commit 897cdf7fe517c9137bb7dfa20e37e32644c5a4fe.
- Nested public implementation evidence: Temporal AI Presence — Architecture-to-Code Evidence Bridge v1.0, https://github.com/Kot141078/advanced-global-intelligence/releases/tag/temporal-ai-presence-implementation-bridge-v1.0, tag commit 60a3e2ae871320c1e4fdf6036e8ba4c069b66117, archive SHA-256 7c7d0e0ad88aa7c49af6134604c1686a59ec3cc5df56dd134439fa10a93c39f7.
- Effective evidence status: TAP-T01, T02, T04, T05, T06, T07, T08, T09 and T10 are PUBLIC_VERIFIED. TAP-T03 is PUBLIC_PARTIAL_WITH_DEPLOYMENT_EXTERNAL_BOUNDARY.
- TAP-T03 boundary: deployment activation, external orchestrator state, production pause/revoke enforcement, and deployment-level witness activation are not fully verified.
- Relation: Temporal AI Presence is not c by default. All valid c-class systems are Temporal AI Presences. Not all Temporal AI Presences are c-class systems.
- Claim ceiling: M4_FULL_PASS=false; TAP-C=NOT CLAIMED. The bridge does not establish consciousness, personhood, full c conformance, universal safety, production readiness, or universal deployment conformance.

## MOT-c v0.1 — Motivational Formation, Reflective Endorsement, and Motivational Custody
- Human page: https://ivankotov.eu/publications/motivational-formation-c-v0-1/
- Machine index: https://ivankotov.eu/publications/motivational-formation-c-v0-1/files/machine/index.json
- Schema.org JSON-LD: https://ivankotov.eu/publications/motivational-formation-c-v0-1/files/schema.org.jsonld
- Version DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.22060517
- GitHub corpus entry: https://github.com/Kot141078/advanced-global-intelligence/tree/mot-c-v0.1/publications/motivational-formation-c-v0-1
- Languages: English, Russian
- License: CC BY 4.0
- Core distinction: reward != preference != task != mandate != goal != motive != obligation != authority.
- Social boundary: the payer of computation does not automatically own the motive; a motive does not automatically create a right to another participant's resources.
- Claim ceiling: does not prove consciousness, phenomenal desire, free will, legal personhood, universal motives, or external authority.
- Corpus bridge: Personality Formation and Time-Shaped Continuity -> Motivational Formation; bounded by L4, witness, resource grounding, and custody distinctions.
